problem: Standard robot navigation stacks (Nav2) treat humans as generic obstacles and ignore social context such as people interacting, so planned paths can cut through human interaction zones.
motivation: Mobile robots operating in human environments need to respect social spaces, such as groups of people interacting. Detecting interactions in real time from RGB-D and feeding them into navigation costmaps allows socially aware paths within the widely used ROS2/Nav2 ecosystem.
key_idea: Detect human interactions in real time with a keypoint-based CNN human detector on RGB-D, localize them in 3D, and insert the resulting interaction zones as semantic layers into Nav2 costmaps so planned paths avoid them.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that pairing lightweight deep-learning perception with semantic costmap layers gives socially aware navigation without changing the planner, and that it can be added as a modular ROS2 package.
method: Human interaction detector: CNN, optimized for embedded GPU inference, using keypoint-based human detection on RGB-D images
3D localization: human detections are combined with depth to place interactions in the 3D scene
Interaction zones: detected human interaction zones are represented as social spaces
Costmap integration: zones are added to Nav2 costmaps so the planner modifies paths around them
Modular ROS2 package (Nav2CAN): designed for easy integration and compatibility with other ROS2 packages

setting.backbone: CNN keypoint-based human detector (details not given in abstract)
setting.action_space: Nav2 planner paths over modified costmaps (velocity commands via the Nav2 stack)
